title: Egyetértek / Nem Értek Egyet — és Minden Együtt

sections.title: Bringing the second half of Unit 29 — and Units 21-29 — together
sections.content: egyetért takes -val/-vel for the person you agree with, exactly like kijön valakivel. Under negation, egyet splits off and lands behind the verb, the same igekötő-style swap as bemegy → nem megyek be: Egyetértek becomes Nem értek egyet. mert and the stronger azért, mert back up an opinion with a reason. That's the last piece of Unit 29 — and with it, the whole review is complete: work and prefixes (21-22), tud/lehet/szabad (23), the past tense (24-25), storytelling (26), the future (27), the conditional (28), and now opinions (29), all ready to combine in one conversation.

sections.title: Agree → Disagree, plus a reason
rows: I think so too. / I don't think so.
In my opinion X, because Y.

items.spanish: Egyetértek Károllyal, a másik szálloda jobb.
items.english: I agree with Károly, the other hotel is better.

items.spanish: Nem értek egyet veled, szerintem a másik terv jobb.
items.english: I don't agree with you, in my opinion the other plan is better.

items.spanish: Szerintem ez a jobb terv, mert olcsóbb.
items.english: In my opinion this is the better plan, because it's cheaper.

items.spanish: Azért nem értek egyet, mert szerintem túl drága.
items.english: That's why I disagree — because in my opinion it's too expensive.

sections.content: By now you have a full toolkit for a whole conversation: talk about your job and your day (21-22), what you can and can't do (23), what happened (24-26), what's coming next (27-28), and what you think about it, backed up with a reason (29).
